decisive_items: Severe emphysema and bullous changes throughout the lungs, left lung lobe greater than right
Right lateral and basilar pneumothorax, approximately 30% in volume
response.rationale: The vignette shows severe emphysema/bullae with a large bulla and pneumothorax in a smoker, consistent with COPD complicated by spontaneous pneumothorax. R6 captures the underlying disease and acute event; R10 only names the pneumothorax without the chronic etiology.

rejected.why: Only describes the pneumothorax, not the underlying emphysema/COPD.
Substance use is present but not the primary cause of the imaging findings.
Substance-induced pneumothorax is less specific; smoking and emphysema are more central.
Cystic lung disease is a broad category; emphysema/bullae are better classified as COPD.
Interstitial lung disease not supported; findings are emphysematous.
Substance use disorder is a comorbidity, not the diagnosis.
PLCH unlikely; no characteristic cysts or nodules, and smoking-related emphysema is more typical.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin level normal, so deficiency excluded.
